dream.title: Dream · The anthill
pages:
His parents are still arguing across the road.
Hugo holds half an ice pop. Meltwater runs down his wrist.

There is an anthill by his shoe.
An ant is dragging a husk into the entrance. It catches. More ants crowd behind it.
dream.journalBody:
The anthill dream again.
The knocking was still there when Hugo woke up. Next door.
dream.fallbackPage: The sound beneath Hugo’s shoe has not stopped.

nightDream.speaker: Dream
yog: Hello, human. You may call me Bubble.

Hugo: ...Hello.
Bubble: You look like a sheet of paper left out in the rain.
Hugo: Thank you.
Bubble: You are welcome.

Hugo watches his scattered fingers.
“Was I... dead just now?”
“No. The loose pieces have been put back. The order may be a little different.”

“What is that thing in the sky?”
“Only a part of it passing by.”
Bubble pauses.
“You may go back. You will remember. The others will not.”

“Will going back help?”
“I do not know.”
Bubble smiles.
“When everything ends, we will meet again.”
replacement:
Hugo lies down. The flat is quiet, except for the filter in the next room.
Then even that stops.

Footsteps cross the bedroom floor. Water drips beside the bed.
“Don’t get up. You’ve had enough.”

It is his own voice.
“I know what to say at the interview. I listened every time.”

Something cold settles across his mouth.
“Rest. I’ll do the difficult part.”
The bedside lamp stays on.

knowledge.ancientBody:
Hugo adjusts the telescope on the fifth-floor roof. Stars bend along a curve.
The curve moves too.
Hugo lets go of the focus ring. His other hand takes longer.
knowledge.windowBody:
Hugo remembers a window on the third floor opposite. The sheet is still hanging there. The window is gone.
He writes it down. The architect can explain later.

telescope.title: Telescope
telescope.nightOnly: Nothing but glare. I’ll try after dark.
telescope.wrongDay: I’ll remember this position tonight. Tomorrow evening I’ll carry the telescope to the roof and get a clearer look.
telescope.wrongDaySecond: I’ll carry the telescope to the roof tonight for a clearer look.
telescope.gainedSuffix: His hand is shaking. Can he still draw the edge?
telescope.repeatSuffix: That edge again. He could try drawing it.
telescope.firstNight:
There should be stars there.
Something’s covering them. The edge is too steady for a cloud.
telescope.recheck:
The clouds have moved on. It’s still there.
Those three stars at the edge are gone now.
Maybe it’s that unusual activity they mentioned. I’ll check again tomorrow night.
telescope.sleepThought:
An hour already… My eyes hurt.
I’ve marked the positions. That’s enough for tonight. I should get some sleep.

firstLoop.news:
The Will Circus arrives Friday. Organizers confirm that all animals have been accounted for.

Miyazaki Sushi opens its 101st branch tomorrow. The first hundred customers receive a commemorative lunch box.

Police advise residents not to give the Triangle Church their address, photograph or hair.

The observatory expects a visible supernova tonight. There is no cause for alarm. Please stop calling the weather hotline.

Unplug the television.

Added with another pen: do not look up to find it.
firstLoop.dayOneCaption: 401 adds another board. Hugo is still in slippers. A clear difference in preparedness.
firstLoop.startledCaption: The hammer stops. Hugo’s prepared complaint cannot find an opening.
firstLoop.boardingCaption: Hugo notices the last nail is bent. The tenant leaves it. Each man lets one thing go.
firstLoop.chapterText:
Hugo moves his eye away from the telescope.
The roof is still quiet. Hugo is not prepared to vouch for that quiet.

bedroom.title: Writing on the desk
bedroom.body:
Carved: the stars did not move. The eye did.
Dust deep in the grooves. Not fresh.

corridor.title: Under the wallpaper
corridor.body:
The boards will not stop it. I just do not want to see it again.
That wallpaper is years old. When was this written?

balcony.title: Seven marks
balcony.body:
Six upright. A seventh across them. Below: do not count.
Too late.

evidence.title: Old observation records
evidence.body: Three months of star positions, times and cloud cover. Several pages show the same field above the balcony.

evidence.title: Balcony telescope
evidence.body: A worn focus ring. Tape marks the north leg. The old observing log uses the same alignment marks.

evidence.title: The leaflet
evidence.body:
Cover windows. Lights off. Unplug the TV.
Added: do not look up to find it.
The pen went through the paper.

evidence.title: Boards over 401
evidence.body:
Even the cracks are covered. The last nail is bent.
Definitely not decorative.

evidence.body:
Hugo adjusts the telescope on the fifth-floor roof. Stars bend along a curve.
The curve moves too.
Hugo lets go of the focus ring. His other hand takes longer.

evidence.title: The opposite window
evidence.body:
Sheet still there. Window gone.
What if Hugo misremembers the sheet?

evidence.title: Water-change Label
evidence.body: A water-change chart is stuck to the cabinet. Hugo made the last tick. A little fish food is stuck beside it.

evidence.title: A Face Under the Scales
evidence.body: On the third day, scales stretch apart around a human face. The mouth moves without a sound.

evidence.title: Where the Tank Used to Be
evidence.body: The moved tank exposes an old ring of dust. A wet trace stops beside the dining stool.

evidence.title: She Remembers the Complaints
evidence.body: She knows Hugo is waiting to hear about work, and that he often says he does not want to go out. He used to say those things to the tank.

evidence.title: Missing pages
evidence.body:
Two torn stubs. Saturday on both sides, same crossed-out number.
Since when was Hugo’s memory that good?

evidence.title: Dust under 403
evidence.body:
Chair scrapes inside. Stops when Hugo knock. Dust under the door undisturbed.
Hope the floor just carries sound.

evidence.title: Note from 401
evidence.body:
Knock twice if you need something.
Come alone.

The note is taped low. Hugo bends to read it. His knees complain first.

evidence.title: The neighbor’s warning
evidence.body:
The tenant told Hugo to go inside, close the windows and leave the television off.
He did not say why.

evidence.title: The missing stars
evidence.body: The first observation: a sharply curved blank patch. The nearby stars stayed in focus.

evidence.title: One hour later
evidence.body: The tripod and field of view stayed fixed. The clouds moved away, but the dark patch remained. Three stars along its edge had disappeared.

evidence.title: What Fish Heard
evidence.body: Fish recalls a night when the water suddenly stung, unlike a water change. She also heard heavy objects being dragged next door while Hugo was out. She does not know what they were. Nothing yet establishes a connection between the water and the noises.

evidence.title: Will Circus
evidence.body: The Will Circus arrives Friday. Organizers confirm that all animals have been accounted for.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Miyazaki Sushi
evidence.body: Miyazaki Sushi opens its 101st branch tomorrow. The first hundred customers receive a commemorative lunch box.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Maintenance handover receipt
evidence.body: One assignment number: a third-night test and seventh-night initiation. Signed by 401. A revocation number is printed at the bottom.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Service-room wiring diagram
evidence.body: 401 draws power from the shaft on a separate circuit. Initiation uses a callback line. A note reads: loss of power is not a revocation.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Search orders
evidence.body: From Day 4, search parties work through addresses across the city. The lists share a dispatch number. The broadcast command terminal is still accepting updates. This is a new city crisis, separate from the bombing.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Operator routing log
evidence.body: The operator left a note: stopping dispatch requires validating the search-list number, then severing the broadcast route at the command terminal. Switching off one radio will not stop it.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Day 6 observation log
evidence.body: The Day 6 log shows the occultation synchronizing with the local observation array. It does not explain the ancient entity, but records when the array begins synchronizing.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Array maintenance manual
evidence.body: The manual contains an emergency shutdown. Identify the synchronized route against the daily observations before shutting it down, rather than blindly destroying the telescope.
evidence.source: Recorded on site in the city

evidence.title: Cooking oil
evidence.body: An ordinary kitchen preparation item.
evidence.source: Actively recorded during the Day 2 investigation

evidence.title: Sealed Maintenance Core
evidence.body: A fictional factory-sealed core, kept closed.
evidence.source: Actively recorded during the Day 2 investigation

evidence.title: Heat-mark leaflet
evidence.body: A fictional maintenance mark links the sealed core to an abstract inventory preparation. No recipe is provided.
evidence.source: Actively recorded during the Day 2 investigation

evidence.title: Pipe Pulse
evidence.body: Three low taps run through the shared shaft. A fresh service mark points below the entrance.
evidence.source: Actively recorded during the Day 2 investigation

evidence.title: Purification Assignment
evidence.body: Remove living things. Area: this building. Deadline: seventh day. Signed: resident of 401. The folded edge has turned white.
evidence.source: Actively recorded during the Day 2 investigation

evidence.title: The tenant’s attack
evidence.body: An arm contraction precedes each lunge. This memory can inform an unnatural ability after an earned return.
evidence.source: Actively recorded during the Day 2 investigation

deductions.title: The obstruction is growing
deductions.body: The same field, an hour apart: more stars have vanished behind the edge. It is not a passing cloud. Its distance and cause are still unknown.

deductions.title: The same curve
deductions.body: The first night’s blank patch and the rooftop sketch share a curved edge. It may have been there before the second night.

deductions.title: What did he know?
deductions.body:
Warning first. Bulletin later.
If he meant the astronomy item, why not say so?

deductions.title: Sealing the door
deductions.body:
Sent me home. Boarded up his own door.
At least it was not just a way to shut me up.

deductions.title: Blocking the view
deductions.body:
Boards cover every crack. The writing says it does not want to see.
Could be a coincidence. Do not speak for him yet.

deductions.title: Another Mouth
deductions.body: Hugo has always filled in the water-change chart himself. This time, when he approaches the tank, a voice answers him. She has understood at least some of what he said.

deductions.title: From the Tank into the Flat
deductions.body: The water marks lead back to the displaced tank. She also remembers what Hugo said through the glass. The person calling him when he woke did not come in through the door.

deductions.title: City search dispatch source
deductions.body: The list number matches the routing log. Stop dispatch at the broadcast terminal.

deductions.title: Synchronized observation route
deductions.body: The log and manual identify the same route. Emergency shutdown is possible.

deductions.title: Sealed preparation pair
deductions.body: The two inventory items match the fictional repair system; the leaflet is still needed.

deductions.title: A single-use prepared tool
deductions.body: Inventory preparation is now available. It consumes the two items without a sanity cost or real construction instructions.

deductions.title: The Triangle and the Assigned Building
deductions.body: The bulletin’s Triangle group is the organization on the third-night order.

deductions.title: Underground Power Source
deductions.body: The assignment and shared-shaft pulse locate the source in the basement service room. The tenant’s defeat will not switch it off.

deductions.title: Power and initiation
deductions.body: The diagram separates household power from the initiation callback. Switching off the basement cabinet will not revoke a scheduled request. The controller remains with 401.

deductions.title: The seventh-night revocation number
deductions.body: The test and initiation share an assignment number. The handover gives the revocation code; the wiring diagram identifies the callback route. The controller must be recovered from 401 before the seventh night.

day3Pages:
Scales stretch around an eye on the flank.

Hugo holds the food.
“Stay still.”

The fish stays still. The mouth makes no sound.
day4Pages:
“You splashed water in.”

Hugo stops.
“When did you start talking?”

“Just now. You were talking about the interview.”

“I was not.”

“You get quieter when you say that.”
day7Pages:
“I could answer your calls.”

Her voice is almost Hugo’s.

“You keep saying you do not want to go out.”

He wants to say something other than thank you or no.
He is a little late.
day5Pages:
She presses a new hand against the glass.

“If I go out, could you rest?”

Hugo remembers saying he did not want another interview. He had not known someone in the tank was keeping track.
day6Pages:
She arranges her hair like Hugo’s.

“Would they recognize me?”

Hugo: Tell me who you want to recognize you.

She does not answer.

Hugo rests it on the surface. The fish moves out of his shadow.
aquarium.sealedBefore:

The fish nudges it once, then swims away.

cult.sound:
Three more blows next door.
Hugo turns over. 401 has apparently not scheduled a day off.
dayOne:
The neighbor stops mid-swing. He looks at Hugo’s slippers, then his face.
“Not been out today?”
Hugo: “How is that your business?”
“It is.”

He moves the hammer to his left hand. Two water bottles stand by the door. One is unopened.
“I need to know who goes out in this building.”
Hugo: “Are you my mother?”
He does not smile.

“Is your television on?”
Hugo: “No.”
“You looked at the stairs when you said that.”
Hugo pauses.
Hugo: “I will look at you next time.”

His hand trembles. A nail drops. He does not bend down.
“Look at the stars last night?”
Hugo: “Why?”
“If not, do not. Go home. Close the window. Leave the television off.”
cult.note:
Knock twice if you need something.
Come alone.

The note is taped low. Hugo bends to read it. His knees complain first.
door:
An eye appears in the crack.
“Who is it?”

“402. From yesterday…”
“Oh. You.”
The eye flicks toward the corridor.

“Go home. They can see us.”
His eye moves past Hugo.
“Water… no, not yet. Sorry.”

Something rustles behind the boards. A little triangle folded from foil squeezes through the crack.
“Don’t unfold it. You can put it in water.”

The eye stays on Hugo.
“Take it. Get back inside.”
The triangle drops onto the sill.
cult.refusal:
Someone holds their breath behind the door.
A moment later, something heavy scrapes across the floor inside.
cult.itemBody:
Several folds of foil. Hugo squeezes it. Something hard inside.
The neighbor said not to unwrap it. So far, a manageable instruction.
cult.lateRefusal:
Through the boards, he seems to be checking with someone.
“This building is mine… Yes, all of it.”
“Anything alive has to go. Nothing alive, nothing to change.”
When Hugo knocks again, the room falls silent.

morning.wake:
…What is he hammering now?
Does the guy in 401 ever sleep?
morning.neighbor: Still hammering next door. Better have a look.
morning.food: …Forget it. I need something to eat.
morning.kitchen: There should still be bread in the fridge.
morning.fridgeOpen:
The TV just turned itself on.
Isn’t the remote still on the table?
morning.afterNews: Hold on. They just mentioned the observatory.
morning.sofa: I could sleep… Not like I have work today.
morning.desk:
Nearly dark already…
That anthill again. I should write it down while I still remember.
morning.writing:
The man next door. The TV. That dream.
What a day.
morning.telescope: The news said it would be visible tonight. Worth trying the telescope.
morning.investigate: Two observations, with positions and times. Compare them.
morning.connect:
The same patch of sky. How much changed?
B  Open the evidence board.
morning.journalBody:
The hammering next door woke Hugo. The tenant of 401 told him to go back inside and leave the TV off.
The TV came on while he opened the fridge. He ate some bread, then slept on the sofa until dusk.
The anthill dream was still with him when he woke.
morning.breadMeal:
Dry.
…Now I’m even sleepier. No job to get to. I’ll lie down for a bit.
fishMorningPages:
Hugo.
Hey… get up a second.

Cold fingers touch his arm.
Someone is crouching beside him. Her hair is dripping.

Hugo: You—
Fish: Don’t kick.
Hugo: …How did you get in?
Fish: The tank.

Hugo stares at her.
Fish: I don’t know either. I didn’t have legs a minute ago.
Hugo: Stay there. I’ll get a towel.

She braces her shoulder against the tank, pushing a little, then resting.
Next comes the scrape of a stool by the dining table.

Fish: I’m sitting here.
Hugo: …Fine. Lift the stool. They’ll hear it downstairs.
She looks down at her feet, then at the stool.

worldEnd.title: Hugo, Who Did Nothing
lines: After the bang, the room comes down on him.
worldEnd.summary:
Ending 01 · Hugo, Who Did Nothing
He never received the gift. He never woke again.

lines: She remembered every worry he had told her.
There was one part she never understood: Hugo had wanted to be heard.

fishGoodChoices: You don’t have to go for me. I’m just venting.
Leave the coat. Help me listen to what he’s doing next door.
fishBadChoices: Then it’s all yours. I’m done with it.
fishGoodReplies:
Fish: Will you still say it?
Hugo: Say what?
Fish: The work stuff.
Hugo: …Probably.
She moves a little closer to Hugo.
Fish: Then leave the pump off.

She puts the coat back on the armrest.
Fish: If I hear something, what do I do?
Hugo: Tell me when I get back. Don’t knock on his door yourself.
Fish: Don’t be long, then.
fishBadReplies:
Fish: Really?
Hugo screws the lid onto the food jar without answering.
She stays by the glass.
Fish: I’ll try, then.

She holds the coat without putting it on.
Fish: All of it?
Hugo: …Yes.
Fish: Then you stay in the flat.
fishAllyPages:
Fish: One night, the water really stung.
Hugo: Was it dirty?
Fish: No. It doesn’t hurt when you change it.
She tilts her head toward the shared wall.
Fish: And he drags things when you’re out. He did it again today.

Hugo: Any more noise?
Fish: Yes. Stopped, then started again.
Hugo: You don’t have to keep watch.
Fish: I haven’t got anywhere else to sit.
She edges the stool half an inch closer to the wall.
expansion.fishHelpBody: Fish recalls a night when the water suddenly stung, unlike a water change. She also heard heavy objects being dragged next door while Hugo was out. She does not know what they were. Nothing yet establishes a connection between the water and the noises.
expansion.bubbleTradeLine: Sanity is not free. Neither is knowledge.
fishChats:
Fish: That bit is wet.
Hugo looks down and moves his foot back.
Hugo: Did the tank spill?
Fish: When you were carrying the bucket.

Fish: You haven’t eaten again?
Hugo: I have.
Fish: The wrapper hasn’t moved.
Hugo glances at the table.
Hugo: …In a minute.

Hugo: Does being called Fish bother you?
Fish: If you called something else, I might not know you meant me.

The same advert comes on.
Fish: He comes here a lot.
Hugo: It’s a recording.
Fish: Oh. That’s why he never changes his clothes.

Hugo stands nearby for a while.
Fish: What is it?
Hugo: Nothing.
She moves over a little.

Fish: You’ve got fish food on you.
Hugo: No, I haven’t.
She looks at his sleeve. He glances down and brushes off a pellet.

Hugo: What did I look like through the glass?
Fish: Wider face.
Hugo: And now?
She looks again.
Fish: About the same.

Hugo switches off the television.
A moment later, Fish closes her mouth too.
Hugo: Were you saying it along with them?
She neither nods nor shakes her head.

Fish: You’ve fed me already.
Hugo: Oh.
He screws the lid back on.
Fish: You made that face last time too.

His phone chimes. Hugo checks it immediately.
Fish waits.
Hugo: Ad.
She doesn’t ask.

Hugo: Have I told you this one?
Fish: Yes.
Hugo: …Never mind, then.
Fish: What happened after? You didn’t finish it last time.

Fish: Don’t knock.
His hand stops in front of the glass.
Hugo: Habit.
Fish: I haven’t gone anywhere.

Hugo: That’s a whale. Not a fish.
Fish: I didn’t ask.
Hugo looks at the television and leaves the rest unsaid.

A plant has tipped sideways.
Hugo reaches to straighten it. Fish watches his hand.
Hugo: What?
Fish: Nothing. Go slowly.

The pump stops.
Fish looks up.
Hugo: Cleaning the filter.
Fish: How long?
Hugo: A few minutes.

Fish: You fell asleep.
Hugo: No, I didn’t.
She points at the mark the sofa left on his cheek.

Hugo draws an arc on the paper, then crosses it out.
Fish: What about that one?
Hugo: Got it wrong.
Fish: I hadn’t finished looking.

Fish suddenly looks at the wall.
Hugo stops to listen too.
Nothing.
Hugo: You heard something?
Fish: A second ago.

Hugo: Going out for a bit.
Fish: Keys.
Hugo pats his pocket and comes back.

She glances at her reflection in the glass, then turns away.
Hugo: What’s wrong?
Fish: Not used to it.

Hugo: Shall I move that stone?
Fish: Don’t.
He puts it back.
After a moment, she adds: There’s something under it.

Hugo: I’m fine.
She watches him.
Hugo: …Really.
She looks down and lets it go.

The key turns. Fish looks toward the door first.
Hugo: It’s me.
Fish: I could tell.

Hugo keeps tapping the edge of the table.
Fish watches him.
Hugo: What?
Fish: You’ve been doing that for ages.
He puts his hand in his pocket.
fishSilentChats: Hugo crouches. The fish sinks to the gravel and faces him through the glass.

“Not checking it today. That’s it.”
He puts the phone face down on his knee. A moment later, he turns it over again.

Too much food.
Hugo scoops with the little net. She follows it, eating a pellet at a time.

“…Sick of it too?”
The fish swims to the other end.
Hugo laughs once, then goes quiet.

The pump hums.
Hugo opens his mouth, then settles for, “Never mind.”

He moves aside to let some light into the tank.
The fish follows his shadow instead.

“Just this for you, then. Easy.”
He puts down the fish food and goes to search the kitchen cupboards.

He says nothing.
The fish hovers by the glass for a while, flicks her tail, and swims away.
apocalypseReunion:
“I’m so glad to see you again, Hugo.”
“Did you get a good look this time?”

Hugo opens his mouth. There is still ash in his throat.
“The others… in the building?”

“Still inside.”
Bubble bends down, inspecting a broken toy.
“But you’re here. See? I didn’t lose you.”

“You knew he would blow up the building?”
“Blow up?” Bubble repeats softly.
“Oh. That’s what you call it.”

“I didn’t give you a little more time.”
“I gave you another turn. They only had this one. You can go back.”

“Back where?”
“The first day. What you remember stays.”
“Your body will be a little older. But there’s still so much of it you can use.”

“And if I still can’t save them?”
“Then try again.”
“You’ll understand a little more. It’s all right if it hurts. You already know when it’s coming.”

“…You think that’s a gift?”
“Of course.”
“I took so long choosing it. Don’t you like it?”

“There. Time to wake up.”
“Keep your eyes open this time, Hugo.”
apocalypseCaptions: No sound reaches this place as the Earth breaks.

entries.title: Will Circus
entries.body: The Will Circus arrives Friday. Organizers confirm that all animals have been accounted for.

entries.title: Miyazaki Sushi
entries.body: Miyazaki Sushi opens its 101st branch tomorrow. The first hundred customers receive a commemorative lunch box.

entries.title: Handover register
entries.body:
Third-night test. Seventh-night initiation. Both lines share a number.
The revocation field is empty. The attendant has signed very carefully.

entries.title: Wiring diagram
entries.body:
A thin callback line runs beside the power circuits.
Hugo traces it to 401. The mains switch does not reach it.

entries.title: Search orders
entries.body:
Addresses, no charges.
The broadcast will explain for them.

entries.title: Broadcast routing
entries.body:
The same words are routed to every street.
Enough voices in unison can sound like agreement.

entries.title: Observation log
entries.body:
Every curve bends at the same second. The instruments are working.
Bad news tends to be punctual.

entries.title: Array manual
entries.body:
Calibrate. Align. Lock.
They gave every step a reassuring name.

entries.title: Return
entries.body: Return to the apartment or street.

entries.title: West · Maintenance office
entries.body: Check the test receipt left by 401.

entries.title: East · Broadcast station
entries.body: Investigate the city search dispatch.

entries.title: Uphill · Observatory
entries.body: Look for the observation logs from Day 6.

entries.title: Street bench: rest 45 minutes
entries.body: Sit for a while. It does not count as sleep.

entries.title: Caretaker
entries.body: “Maintenance is west. The handover sheet? On the cabinet. Just do not sign my name.”
entries.locked: He avoids your eyes, clutching his keys.

entries.title: Service notice
entries.body: A page is missing from the 401 service record. The last entry bears the basement equipment-room stamp.

entries.title: Stop city search dispatch
entries.body: The tape keeps turning. CITY RELAY glows on the console. A clear cover guards the stop switch.

entries.title: Shut the synchronized observation route
entries.body: Every mirror points at the same coordinates. A faded calibration table hangs beside the emergency lever.

entries.title: Escape the exposed space
entries.body: Reach the far exit and evade the pursuers.

entries.title: Perceptual filter torn
entries.body:
The flat world is ripped apart.
It is wet underneath. Something is running toward you.

entries.title: The filter closes
entries.body:
The split closes. The street is flat again.
You still remember what was underneath.

entries.title: Night clerk
entries.body: “Coffee is cold. Wait for the next pot if you want it hot.”

entries.title: Cat feeder
entries.body: “Not eating today. Keeps looking upstairs.”

days: Day 1: Complete the apartment introduction. Notice the four original bulletins.
Day 2: Enter the street from floor 1. Record the handover and wiring diagram. Meet Bubble after rooftop observation.
Day 3: The neighbor tests the device. A face appears beneath the scales.
Day 4: The fish begins speaking. Listen before deciding what she means.
Day 5: Stop the city dispatch at the broadcast terminal. Avoid patrol sightlines.
Day 6: Compare observation logs with the array manual.
Day 7: Stop the purification device before midnight.
Preserve the building to finish the first stage.
crisis: On the fifth night, districts across the city are sealed.
The same search list travels through the broadcast route. Hugo’s address is on it.
Dispatch was not stopped. Hugo does not survive the search.

entries.title: Again
entries.body:
There is no hat left to remove.
His fingers search the edge of his forehead for a zip that is already torn away.

entries.title: Initiation controller
entries.body: An old controller. The button is polished smooth. Nobody ever labelled a cancel button.
Inspect controller · E

entries.title: Seven Days · First Stage Complete
entries.body:
The neighbor reads his own name from the original order.
This time, he says revoke.

The light goes out. Hugo keeps holding his wrist until it stops crawling toward the button.

entries.title: Seven Days · First Stage Complete
entries.body:
The broadcast reads the revocation number, then every floor.
Doors open one by one.

Hugo has never heard so many people in this building.
Perhaps that was what the list found objectionable.

entries.title: The unfinished sentence
entries.body:
“I heard you,” the neighbor says.

Hugo has not spoken.

His jaw slips sideways. One hand chases the other to hold the hat down. Something beneath the brim starts knocking.
Take one step back.
1–4 choose · R record

entries.title: He does not let go
entries.body:
“Don’t move.”

Hugo cannot tell who he means.

The wrist bends the wrong way. He releases his forehead. Not the controller.

entries.title: Still waiting
entries.body:
The light is still on.
Someone has to answer the last line on the handover receipt.
Use the confirmed receipt number to revoke the seventh-night request.
Make him read the revocation from the original order.
Revoke the request through the confirmed broadcast route, then warn the residents to leave.
Keep the controller and check the records.

entries.title: Crowbar
entries.body: A rusted crowbar. Might open a few heads.

entries.title: Cooking oil
entries.body:
A little oil clings to the bottle.
Not enough for supper. Plenty for a bad idea.

entries.title: Sealed repair core
entries.body:
An old repair core from the bathroom cabinet. A faded flame marks its casing.
The leaflet calls it a safety device. Leaflets rarely take responsibility.

entries.title: Ember case
entries.body:
A sealed little case that remembers being fire.
One use. Hopefully enough.

entries.title: Invitation
entries.body:
A triangle pressed into one corner. No date.
They must assume it is only a matter of time.

entries.title: Knocking in the wall
entries.body:
A tap every few seconds. Upstairs and downstairs answer in turn.
Not a leak. More like a roll call.
It has gone quiet inside. The door is still locked.

entries.title: Force entry
entries.body: Use the crowbar and enter.

entries.title: Knock
entries.body: Knock. Ask about the call.

entries.title: Basement service door
entries.body: A compact service room below the entrance landing.

entries.title: Return to entrance landing
entries.body: Leave the service room.

entries.title: Return to hallway
entries.body: Leave apartment 401.

entries.title: Speak to the neighbor
entries.body: He is still a human being.

entries.title: Paper on the table
entries.body: A triangle is printed at the edge of the paper.

entries.title: The tenant blocks the desk
entries.body: His hand pins the page. “You have not answered my question.”

entries.title: Resident of 401
entries.body:
He presses a hand to his hat. The paper on the table is turned face down.

“How much did you hear?”

entries.title: Calm
entries.body: I am not here to hurt you. Tell me what happened.

entries.title: Threaten
entries.body: Turn it off. Now. Do not make me hurt you.

entries.title: Prior-loop knowledge
entries.body: The order assigns this building to you. I have seen it before.

entries.title: The tenant of 401
entries.body:
“A test tomorrow. The clearing on the seventh.”

Hugo: Clearing what?

“Things that change.”

His forefinger curls into his palm. His other hand takes a while to straighten it.

entries.title: Listen
entries.body: What did they promise you?

entries.title: Leave
entries.body: I will step back.

entries.title: The same triangle
entries.body:
“Living things change.”

He slides the paper over, covering his own name.

“Empty containers do not. This building is mine. Clean by the seventh day.”

Hugo: You are alive too.

“That is why I have to hurry.”

entries.title: Accept
entries.body: Accept the invitation, without ending the investigation.

entries.title: Refuse
entries.body: I will not join. I will not hurt you either.

entries.title: Deceive
entries.body: Pretend to join; use the known assignment number as proof.

entries.title: Keep investigating
entries.body: Let me read the assignment myself.

entries.title: A signature
entries.body:
He offers the invitation. His fingers clamp down as Hugo touches it.

“Don’t be afraid. Once you sign, we’re on the same side.”

Under the table, his other hand slowly closes into a fist.

entries.title: No signature needed
entries.body:
“You don’t have to sign.”

He nods twice. The third time, he cannot stop.

“Don’t look at me. Not yet.”

entries.title: The same side
entries.body:
Hugo recites the assignment number.

“So you are one of us.”

The neighbor laughs. The sound stops several seconds before his mouth does.

entries.title: Reality breaks
entries.body: His fear becomes an attack. The flat room opens around the same furniture.
Finish the sentence.

entries.title: Purification assignment
entries.body:
401. Service shaft. A test on the third night; activation on the seventh.
An entire building lives between those two dates.

entries.title: Handover archive
entries.body:
Two receipts share a number.
The third-night copy says TEST. The seventh-night copy is signed only: 401.

Hugo: The equipment is downstairs. The decision is upstairs.

entries.title: The working cabinet
entries.body:
The seals are intact. The noise inside does not stop because Hugo stands in front of it.

The maintenance plate reads: LOCAL POWER LOSS DOES NOT CANCEL A SCHEDULED REQUEST.
Hugo: Thorough after-sales service.

entries.title: Isolate assigned circuit
entries.body: Isolate only the assigned circuit; preserve residential supply.

entries.title: Lock out source
entries.body: Lock out the verified source.

entries.title: First action complete
entries.body: The 401 indicator dies. The residential line stays lit.

entries.title: Investigation required
entries.body: Hugo stops. The wire numbers do not match. Guessing is not enough.

entries.title: Source still powered
entries.body: The bar will not move. Current still hums inside.

entries.title: Use the basement source
entries.body: This is only a records cabinet. The last service stamp belongs to the basement equipment room.

entries.title: The building survives
entries.body:
The pulse stops.
Upstairs, someone turns on a tap. Someone still expects tomorrow.

entries.title: The assigned building
entries.body:
On the seventh night, the device starts on time.
The floor lifts. The walls split. The last closing door cannot keep out the fire.

entries.title: Behind the opened door
entries.body:
He comes closer.
Hugo never hears the rest.

{0} added to inventory.

entries.body: Recorded.

entries.body: Already in the notebook.

entries.body: E / 1 Take the item
R Record · Enter / Esc Close

entries.body: Prepare the sealed tool after confirming the deduction.

entries.title: Service wiring diagram
entries.body:
The diagram shows 401 fed separately through the shaft. Residential supply runs on another line.
Someone circled them in different colours.

entries.title: Aftermath
entries.body:
Neighbor: The pulse stopped. Was that you?
Hugo: The building is still here.
He folds the invitation and no longer calls the order inevitable.

entries.title: Aftermath
entries.body: A long breath comes from inside. Nobody answers.

entries.title: Taken in this life
entries.body: Added to inventory.

entries.title: Shoulder eye open
entries.body: The shoulder eye is open. {0:0.0} seconds remain. The sanity cost has been paid.

entries.title: Hugo · Day Two
entries.body: The flat feels stuffy. A walk might help. See what is happening outside.

entries.title: He takes off his hat
entries.body:
“Warm in here.”
Under the hat, half the head has stopped being a head.

entries.title: Cognitive contamination · Sanity −20
entries.body:
Hugo understands, suddenly, whose eyes the hat was covering.

The perceptual filter tears. Reality shows its wet underside.

entries.title: The filter tears again
entries.body: The hat leaves his head. The old wound leaves memory.

entries.title: Brain cast
entries.body: His hand reaches behind his head. Move away from where he is looking.

entries.title: Entangled
entries.body: Warm neural tissue tightens. {0:0.0} seconds until you can pull yourself out of this thought.

entries.title: Kick
entries.body: He puts his weight on one leg. The other has plans.

entries.title: Repair leaflet
entries.body:
The leaflet at the bottom shows oil, a flame-marked repair core and a sealed case.
“For emergencies.” Smaller print than the warning.

entries.title: Exit
entries.body: E Leave for the street

entries.title: Miyazaki Sushi · Inside
entries.body:
The tables are neatly set. Every mouth seems to be waiting.
WASD Move · Mouse Look · E Leave at the door

entries.title: Will Circus · Inside
entries.body:
The curtain is closed. The sounds inside the cages have taken their seats.
WASD Move · Mouse Look · E Leave at the door

entries.title: Outside 401
entries.body:
“Third night, a test first. The whole building... seventh day. Nobody left behind.”

The voice drops. Hugo cannot hear the rest.

He takes his hand off the door. Ask first.

entries.title: Kitchen cupboard
entries.body: The door sticks. A service diagram on it shows oil, a flame-marked repair core and a sealed case.
E / 1 Open cupboard

entries.title: Resident of 401
entries.body:
“Were you on the phone?”

A pause. “Maintenance.”

“I heard you say the whole building.”

The chain rattles. “Come in, then. Not out here.”
1. Go inside and ask
Enter / Esc Close
Left mouse Strike · Shift Sprint · Ctrl Crouch
Ask about the foil triangle by the door.

entries.title: The phone lights up
entries.body:
Neighbor: Come over a moment.

Hugo: If you need salt, I am out too.

Neighbor: I think... something is wrong with me.
Go to 401.
Give me a moment. I will turn the light off.

entries.title: 401 · Late night
entries.body:
Two cups. One upside down. The hammer has been pushed to the corner. The radio keeps singing.

He sits with his back to Hugo.
“You came. Is the door shut?”

His right eye jerks.
What happened to your eye?
Stay seated. I am here.
You said clean it out. Clean what?
Watch him.
That is not tiredness. How long?
Back toward the door.

entries.title: He tries to smile
entries.body:
“Nothing. A little tired.”

The eye moves again. Half his face follows.

Hugo: That sounded rehearsed.

“Do not... stare at me.”

His hand covers his eye. His shoulder rises on its own.

entries.title: The doorway
entries.body:
The chair falls. A thin sound comes from the light.

“I do not want this.”

He stands. His body reaches the door before he does.

“Go.”

Hugo: You need to move first.

He cannot.

entries.title: Not over yet
entries.body:
Left mouse attack · Shift sprint · Ctrl crouch · Q dodge
G uses a prepared tool; E escapes at the door.

Hugo: Make him stop. Or let me leave.
He can be hurt. The cold light at the door is still on.

entries.title: The corridor
entries.body:
Hugo wakes on cold tiles. The lock of 401 clicks.

He touches his neck. Still there.

“Do not come back,” someone says inside.
Locked. The footsteps inside recede.
Wait a moment, then knock again.
Continue.
Choose with number keys or click.

entries.title: 401 · Day Seven
entries.body:
The neighbor holds an old controller, still wearing its third-night test label.

Hugo: Put it down.
Neighbor: I’ve been trying.

His thumb stays on the button. His wrist slowly turns toward Hugo.
Keep your eyes on the controller.
“You’re one of the things they want cleared.”
“People are still here. Let them leave.”
Back toward the door.

entries.title: The blank field
entries.body:
Hugo turns the controller over.
The receipt is still unconfirmed. One button does not necessarily mean one service.

entries.title: Words fail
entries.body:
“You have not read it.”

He pins the assignment to the table. Hugo is still missing something that might make him listen.

entries.title: Footsteps in the corridor
entries.body:
The residents follow Hugo away from the doorway.

The building is not safe yet. The device is still humming.

entries.title: Seven Days · First Stage Complete
entries.body:
The controller’s light goes out.

Someone in the hall asks whether the power is out.
Hugo sits against the wall.
“More of a cancelled service.”

This time, he waits for the answer.
Return to the title screen.

entries.title: Put the foil in?
entries.body:
This irreversibly stops the fish’s changes for this journey. She will not speak, become human or become a companion.

Hugo holds his hand above the water.
Put it in.
Keep it for now.

entries.title: The test stops
entries.body:
One indicator dies. Another lights up.

This is not the last one. The handover book still has a signature box for Day Seven.

entries.title: Missed calls
entries.body:
A former colleague asks about dinner. The landlord asks about rent. His mother only says: “Call when you wake up.”

Hugo puts the phone face down. Socks first.

entries.title: Fish food
entries.body:
Hugo drops in two flakes.
“Missed the interview again. Saved the bus fare.”

The fish swims to the glass. He swallows the rest.

entries.title: The old telescope
entries.body:
The focus ring has lost its paint. He used to talk beside it until somebody asked him to keep his voice down.

Nobody asks today.

entries.title: A light behind the door
entries.body:
The light in 401 is still on. Two hammer blows, a pause, then two more.

Hugo almost calls back, “I heard you.” Instead he walks more quietly.

entries.title: Morning outside
entries.body:
Someone feeds a cat. The night clerk finishes a cold coffee from a paper cup.

Hugo checks his phone. Perhaps there is still time to answer somebody today.

entries.title: Two cups
entries.body:
Hugo remembers being asked if he had eaten. He was staring at the hammer.

Some questions take a while to hear.

entries.title: Before the call
entries.body:
The hammer in 401 stops.

The silence makes Hugo look up.

entries.title: The pipe
entries.body:
A small tap comes from the pipe. It did not come from upstairs.

Hugo listens. His phone is still dark.

entries.title: A test inside the wall
entries.body:
A short pulse runs down the shaft. The building does not fall.

Someone seems to be checking a connection.

entries.title: Addresses on the radio
entries.body:
The radio repeats street names. The last is nearby.

The caretaker brings his chair inside.

entries.title: An unanswered call
entries.body:
The neighbor’s phone rings until it stops.

Hugo does not call again. He watches the patch of screen that was lit.

entries.title: Do not come back tonight
entries.body:
A corner of paper sticks out of 401.
“Do not come back tonight.”
The last letter tore the paper.

entries.title: The signature box
entries.body:
The last box is signed. Today’s date.

Hugo suddenly does not want to know whether the hand hesitated.

entries.title: The entrance
entries.body:
Someone pounds on the entrance below. Nobody shouts abuse.

That makes Hugo want to go down more than shouting would.

entries.title: Seven minutes
entries.body:
The footsteps below gradually stop.

Hugo watches the clock. There is still time. Less of it.

entries.title: Sounds in the building
entries.body:
Footsteps stop outside. After a while, they move on.

Hugo takes his ear away from the door.

Hugo looks at the window and forgets what he was about to do.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
The television flickers. A pipe answers.

Hugo looks at the window and forgets what he was about to do.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
The television flickers. A pipe answers.

Hugo looks at the window and forgets what he was about to do.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
The television flickers. A pipe answers.

Hugo looks at the window and forgets what he was about to do.

Bubble: Hello, human. The same morning again.
Hugo: At least I know which switch to leave alone.

Return to Day Seven, 07:00. Keep memories, device knowledge and current items. The final ignition resets. Your body ages by one loop.

entries.title: Outside the door
entries.body:
Someone knocks downstairs. The call to 401 connects.

“You had better come over.”

This time he does not ask if Hugo ate.

entries.title: Day Two · Morning
entries.body:
Hugo hears the hammer again.

Memories, recorded deductions and current items remain. The night encounter and capture count reset. Your body ages by one loop.

He looks at his phone. He still has not returned that call.

entries.title: Resident of 401
entries.body:
His hand grips the brim. He leaves the hammer alone.

“Put that down. We can still talk.”

He pushes the paper to the table’s edge.
“Read it. Then go.”

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
His phone lights up. An old colleague asks about dinner.
Hugo types half a yes, then turns the phone over.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
Two more knocks next door.
“I am awake,” Hugo tells the wall. It does not sound reassured.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
His mother sends a photograph of dinner.
He zooms in for a while. Writes: Looks good.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
A sentence breaks off in the television static.
He turns it down. Not because he understood.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
The refrigerator stops humming.
Only then does he notice he was listening for something else.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
The interview reminder has expired.
The fish rises and touches the glass.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
It is still light outside. The window already looks like a black mirror.
He moves aside to stop blocking his own view.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
Someone once asked what he saw through the telescope.
He answered at great length. Eventually they stopped asking.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
A line of an old song leaks through the wall.
The hammer lands before the chorus.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
A chair scrapes overhead.
Hugo counts the floors again. There is only the roof up there.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
He opens his contacts without thinking.
The bright screen feels like an answered call. He has not dialed.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
Light still shows under 401.
He softens his footsteps, then feels rude for doing it.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
Someone downstairs bought two breakfasts.
One stays in their hand all the way home.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
A cup touches a table inside 401.
Before Hugo can speak, someone says, “Wait.”

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
His phone asks how he slept.
He deletes fine. There is no shorter answer.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
The neighbor pushes the hammer farther away.
Less a threat than a precaution against reaching for it.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
Have you eaten? The question stays with him.
Harder to answer than any slogan.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
A pipe knocks once. Much later, again.
He cannot help knocking back.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
401 appears in his recent calls.
He saves it as Neighbor. Leaves out Dangerous Person.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
Someone stands in the corridor holding a bowl.
When Hugo looks up, they have gone inside.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
His phone brightens, then dims.
He practices “Do you need help?” It sounds like a sales call.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
The old song cuts off.
He waits for the next line and realizes he knows it.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
Something brushes the floor inside 401.
Not a hammer. Hammers do not hesitate.

entries.title: A moment
entries.body:
He arranges his questions in order.
The first is always too long. He never writes the last.
